text: Truncated at a finite history and degree, NVAR is mathematically equivalent to which classical construction?
choices: A truncated Volterra series (equivalently, ridge regression with a polynomial kernel on lagged inputs)
A random Fourier-feature approximation of the RBF kernel
A Kalman filter with a linear Gaussian state-space model
A principal-component analysis of reservoir states
explanation: NVAR with history k and degree d is exactly a Volterra series truncated at order d over a (k+1)-step window; its readout equals kernel ridge regression with the polynomial kernel (c + φ·φ')^d. The random-Fourier/RBF picture (option 1) describes the ESN's random-feature approximation, the complementary view — not NVAR. Options 2 and 3 are unrelated linear/statistical tools.
